Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 99a0e4fbfc11884c7845237a39ad7b6a1bf6c826` → `packageMentionDocs`.

L1: REWORK (one must-fix, a record only; the code is accepted)
Head-sha: 429ee81c919cc60107bfaa016ec0fce21700aac8

This is the first L1 on this PR. I read the full diff against the merge base `aef42cba4e`: 17 files, +414 / −42. I also read the card, premise correction 6970082809, claim 6971069096, amendment 6973523661 and the announcement 6974115233.

**The fix, against the corrected scope.**
- `RecordDetailsBody` wraps its `DetailView` in `EmptySectionsLineContext.Provider value`.
- `DetailView` draws `EmptySectionsLine` when that context or `useDefaultRecordPage()` is on and the body has no `sectionGroups`. That is the one gate that changed, and the existing `EmptySectionsLine` is reused unchanged, so there is no new design.
- The context sits in `defaultRecordPage.ts` beside its siblings. It is not re-exported from the barrel (`index.tsx` changes only the registry's `sections` description), and it is not a `DetailView` prop or a schema key. That keeps it a renderer face, as ADR-0085 has it, and adds no metadata key.
- The `detail-view` node, the drawer and a direct React caller read the default `false` and keep `EmptySectionsFold`.

**Contract prose and its mirrors.**
- The `hideEmpty` `describe()` and doc comment in `component.zod.ts` now say that, read-only, a kept all-empty section is named in the body's closing line first, and that expanding the line draws it as its heading plus one fold row. That matches the code. No key, shape or default moves.
- The same sentence is carried, consistently, by `@object-ui/types` (`RecordDetailsComponentProps`, `DetailViewSection`, which also states the `detail-view` difference), the registry's `sections` input, the README, and the three regenerated mirrors: `sdui.manifest.json`, `scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json`, `component.mdx` and `record.mdx`. The generation gates are green.
- Whether that restatement of the ruled rendering (ruling C on objectui#13386, kept here as the expanded face) is right is the separate L2's question, not mine.

**Shape and scope.**
- `Fixes #35019` is on the first card line, and the corrected scope is delivered whole. No closing keyword sits next to another open card, and there is no `content/docs/releases/` change.
- `check-governed-merges --pr 35161`: not governed (0 of 17 paths), under the 3,000-line threshold.
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right. No accept set or authorable value moves, and the one new name is module-internal.
- The changeset bumps `plugin-detail`, `types` and `spec` at `patch`, and is new, not on `main`. I checked each sentence against the diff:
  - "used to draw every field group the page keeps with `hideEmpty: false` as its own bordered card" is the old authored-page path.
  - "every `record:details` body does what the default record page already did" is the context gate.
  - "An omitted key still hides an all-empty group outright, and such a group is not named in the line" is pinned.
  - "Edit mode … a print page" is pinned.
  - "A standalone `detail-view` … still folds a body whose groups are all empty into one row" is the CONTROL pin.
  - "No metadata key, value or default changes" matches the diff.

**Tests and evidence.**
- `EmptySectionsLine.authoredPage-35019.test.tsx` has 10 cases through the real `RecordDetailsRenderer`, with no default-page context and the HotCRM opportunity's groups as the fixture. They cover:
  - the line, its count and its names;
  - the partly-filled group's own fold row;
  - expand and collapse in authored order;
  - reveal plus a double-click into inline edit, which is the card's 就地编辑 acceptance;
  - edit mode;
  - an all-empty body;
  - the `hideEmpty` default;
  - a print page;
  - two CONTROL cases on a standalone `DetailView`.
- Ablation: the gate was restored to `onDefaultRecordPage &&`. That turned 7 of 10 red, and the 3 that stayed green are the ones that hold either way. The restore was verified (blob == HEAD, empty diff).
- The two existing pins that asserted the old authored face (`record-details.emptySectionDefault.test.tsx` and `record-details.hideEmptyRetired-7129.test.tsx`) now assert the line, expand it, and then assert the same heading plus fold row. The red set before the update was exactly those two files.
- Local runs: plugin-detail 3,470 tests and the spec suites 417, both green. `dispatch-gates`: 123 derived, 123 run, all exit 0.

**CI at this head**, from check-runs: 61 success, 9 skipped, none failed or in progress.

#### Must-fix
- **M1. Two changed paths are outside the amended file surface.**
  - The paths are `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/__tests__/record-details.emptySectionDefault.test.tsx` and `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/__tests__/record-details.hideEmptyRetired-7129.test.tsx`.
  - Claim 6971069096 allows only new test files named for the card. Amendment 6973523661 lists the prose, mirror and context files, but not these two existing pins.
  - The PR body names them under "Beyond the claim's file surface" with the right reason: they pinned the face this card changes, and the red set proves it. The claim record does not name them.
  - Fix: post a second claim amendment on #35019 that adds the two paths with that reason. No new head is needed. I'll read the amendment alone and ACCEPT on it at this head.

#### Should-fix
None.

#### Notes
- **N1.** The PR body says a comment in app-shell's `RecordDetailView` still lists "the empty-sections line" among the faces only the synthesized page draws. That comment is now false, but it is another package and a comment only. It fits a loose-ends card.
- **N2. NOT MEASURED, as declared.** This was not browser-verified on the HotCRM opportunity page. The pins drive the real renderer with that page's groups, which I accept for an M-sized renderer gate.
- **Owed after L1, not mine.** The L2 contract review of the `component.zod.ts` describe at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, at this head, which your area runs.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `429ee81c919cc60107bfaa016ec0fce21700aac8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts + ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/EmptySectionsFold.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/defaultRecordPage.ts, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx, ui/packages/types/src/views.ts, ui/packages/types/src/record-components.ts
Security-touching: no

Inputs read: card #35019 (body and all 6 comments, including the premise correction 6970082809, the claim, the dev report and claim amendment 1), PR #35161 (body, 17-file list, net diff against `main`), and the check-runs on this head: 61 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. Nothing was checked out, built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set: unchanged — right.** The only hunk in `packages/spec/src` rewrites the `describe()` string and the doc comment of `RecordDetailsProps.sections[].hideEmpty`. The schema expression stays `z.boolean().optional()`; no key, type, default or refinement moves. `Spec property liveness` and `Type Check · source gates` are green on the head.
- **Generated mirrors: right.** `content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx` carries the new describe text verbatim; `sdui.manifest.json`, `scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json` and `content/docs/ui/components/record.mdx` move with the registry description. The gates that own them (`Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Build Docs`) are green.
- **Public surface: no new export — right.** `EmptySectionsLineContext` is declared in `defaultRecordPage.ts` and is not re-exported: the barrel's only line for that module is still `export { DefaultRecordPageContext } from './defaultRecordPage'`, and the `index.tsx` hunk is the one registry `description` string. No `DetailView` prop and no `DetailViewSchema` key is added.
- **Rendered behaviour: changes, and is declared.** Every `record:details` body now folds its kept all-empty sections into `EmptySectionsLine`; on those bodies the whole-body fold (`EmptySectionsFold`) is no longer reachable. This is the scope ruled on the card (6970082809: "draw the same `EmptySectionsLine` on authored `record:details` pages too ... No new design and no new metadata key"), and the changeset states it.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/35019-empty-groups-line.md`: `@object-ui/plugin-detail`, `@object-ui/types` and `@objectstack/spec`, each `patch`. That matches what publishes: spec and types ship prose only; plugin-detail ships a read-only rendering change with no API, prop or metadata change. `Check Changeset` is green.
- `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and in the changeset is correct: no declared capability is narrowed, nothing an author can write is refused or reinterpreted, and `hideEmpty` keeps its keep-or-disappear meaning in both polarities. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct for the same reason.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty; nothing to answer.
- Deviation, file-surface breach: answered by claim amendment 1 (6973523661). Read against the diff, the amendment's account holds: the files outside the original surface are the context and its provider (inside the ruled scope), restated prose, and regenerated mirrors. No behaviour sits in them beyond the provider.
- Deviation, L2 face found: this record.
- Deviation, first push before `overlap-check`: no effect on the head under review.
- Deviation, `origin/main` advanced after the last merge: the review reads the three-dot diff at this head; the queue's own merge check owns staleness.
- Deviation, not browser-verified: accepted for this face. The 10 new tests mount the real `RecordDetailsRenderer`, and `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI` and all 16 `Test UI` shards are green on the head.
- Out-of-scope notes (stale app-shell `RecordDetailView` comment; the imprecise CONTROL name in `recordPageV3Face-27055.test.tsx`; the default page's `{ group }` sections resolving `hideEmpty` to `true`): outside this diff, read and not reviewed. None contradicts the contract text under review. The first two are comment and test-name drift and can ride a follow-up.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; the fold reads the record already in the host context.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` (hits).** The restated `describe()` was read sentence by sentence against the tree at this head:

- "disappears when ALL its fields are empty (renderer default: on ...)" — unchanged, and still true: `record-details.tsx` resolves `hideEmpty: s.hideEmpty ?? true`, `DetailSection` returns nothing for such a section, and `isFoldableEmptySection` returns `false` on `hideEmpty === true`, so a hidden section is never named or counted in the line.
- "in read-only mode the details body names it in the one line that closes the body, beside every other all-empty section kept this way" — true. `RecordDetailsRenderer` wraps its `DetailView` in `EmptySectionsLineContext`; the schema it synthesizes carries `sections` (or the direct-`fields` fallback) and never `autoTabs`, `tabs` or `sectionGroups`, so it always reaches the non-tab sections block, where `emptySectionsAsLine && !schema.sectionGroups?.length` selects `EmptySectionsLine`. The line is emitted after every drawn section.
- "expanding that line renders each in its place as its heading plus one fold row ..." — true. Revealed, the line maps every section through the same `renderSection` at its own index, and `DetailSection`'s `foldAllEmptySection` draws the heading plus the fold row (ruling C, objectui#13386), unchanged.
- "in edit mode it renders every field as an editable row" — true. `isEditing` empties the folded set in `EmptySectionsLine`, and `foldAllEmptySection` is off in edit mode. A print page is handled the same way and prints every row, as before.

The describe implements the card's ruling and agrees with its first and only consumer. The emptiness reading in the line (`hasCellValue(data?.[name] ?? field.value)`) is the one `DetailSection` folds by, over the same `fields` array after the security and hidden-field folds, so the line and the sections cannot disagree about which section is empty; a section those folds empty to zero fields is neither named nor drawn.

**Implementing files.**

- `renderers/record-details.tsx`: the provider wraps exactly the one `DetailView` this renderer mounts; the comment on the `hideEmpty` default is restated consistently with the describe. Agrees.
- `DetailView.tsx`: the gate is `inRecordDetailsBody || onDefaultRecordPage`, so the default page keeps what it drew, and a bare `DetailView` (context default `false`) keeps `foldEmptySections`. The `autoTabs` branch is untouched and unreachable from `record:details`. Agrees.
- `EmptySectionsFold.tsx`: doc comment only; its statement that the line takes the whole-body fold's place where every section is empty matches the gate. Agrees.
- `defaultRecordPage.ts`: the context defaults to `false` and its docblock's claim of being module-internal is true at this head. Agrees.
- `index.tsx`, `ui/packages/types/src/record-components.ts`, `ui/packages/types/src/views.ts`: prose mirrors of the describe; consistent with it, subject to N3.

Attempts to break it, and what they found:

- Loading: `DetailView` returns its skeleton while `loading`, so the line does not flash over an unloaded record.
- Nested bodies: no other `DetailView` is mounted beneath the provider in `DetailSection` or the field renderers, so the context does not leak into a body it was not meant for.
- A partly-filled section is never folded (`fields.some(hasCellValue)`), so the card's item 2 holds.
- A malformed section turns the fold off for itself (`try`/`catch`, non-array `fields`) and still fails inside its own `SectionBoundary`.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits (none affects correctness or the contract; none needs a change on this head):

- N1 (nit) — The describe says the body "names" the section. A kept section with no `label` has no name to print: the line counts it ("1 empty section · Expand") and prints no name for it. The count and the expand behaviour are right; only the verb is loose for untitled sections. Accepted deviation, or one clause in a later prose pass.
- N2 (nit) — The reader's remembered "show empty fields" choice (`recordPagePreferences`, per object) does not open the line, and the line's own expanded state is local and not remembered. A reader with that choice on used to see a kept all-empty group's fields directly on an authored page; they now expand the line on each visit, after which the fields show at once. This is the shipped line's behaviour and the ruling asked for no new design, and the PR's acceptance notes say the fields are one click further. Worth a follow-up card on whether the remembered choice should open the line.
- N3 (nit) — `DetailViewSection.hideEmpty` in `ui/packages/types/src/views.ts` now reads "a `detail-view` body draws them in place". A `detail-view` body under the default record page context also draws the line (the `onDefaultRecordPage` arm of the gate), as it did before this PR. Pre-existing behaviour, slightly over-general sentence. Accepted deviation.

## Contract review brief — PR #35161 @ `429ee81c919cc60107bfaa016ec0fce21700aac8` (card #35019)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is

on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:

  · PR #35161: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `429ee81c919cc60107bfaa016ec0fce21700aac8`
  · the check-runs on `429ee81c919cc60107bfaa016ec0fce21700aac8`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — if a `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` and the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/49ef2e5d-7385-538e-818f-5529608e498c/scratchpad/pr-35161/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.
